section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: FileSwitch has been extended with support for enumerating file handles, a catalogue filename width, IOCtl operations, and a reminder about the redeclaration of filing systems.

subsection.title: Enumerate Handles
subsection.p: A reason code is available within FileSwitch version 2.44 onward to enumerate file handles. This allows clients to obtain information on open files using a defined interface rather than relying on knowledge of the earlier restriction within FileSwitch of 255 file handles, allocated sequentially downward from 255. This reason code is used by clients wishing to enumerate open file handles. Clients should be aware that filing system operations may occur during the enumeration process and should take appropriate action. See .

subsection.title: Catalogue filename width
subsection.p: A variable, FileSwitch$NameWidth, can be set to give the width of filenames in the *Cat display. It has a minimum value of 12, and a maximum value of 255. This can be set at any time and will be read per-use of *Cat. It is present in all versions of FileSwitch since RISC OS 4.

subsection.title: IOCtl operations
subsection.p: From FileSwitch 2.36 onward support has been added for IOCtl calls. These allow 'control' commands from the client opening the file. An OS_Args reason code has been added to support this, and a new bit added to the extra filing system information word. See . This operation will be passed to the FileSystem Args entry as reason code 11.
The IOCtl parameter block takes the following form :

offset-table.offset:
Flags:
IOCtl reason code IOCtl group code:
Serial group operations Parallel group operations Generic group operations
Reserved (must be 0) Set to read data Set to write data

subsubsection.title: Serial IOCtl operations
subsubsection.p: The following serial IOCtl operation reason codes are defined for serial devices :

value-table.value: One word containing the baud rate (bits per second)

One word containing flags indicating data format:
Data length (5,6,7 or 8) Number of stop bits (1 or 2) Parity encoded as:
No parity Even parity Odd parity Reserved
Reserved

One word containing the handshaking type:
No handshaking RTS/CTS handshaking XON/XOFF handshaking DTR/DSR handshaking Reserved
Size of buffer used for transfers
Trigger for handshaking or upcall notification

One word containing flags:
DTR (read/write) RTS (read/write) Reserved (read/write) CTS (read only) DSR (read only) RI (read only) DCD (read only) FIFOs enabled (read only) Reserved (read only)
Number of bytes in FIFO before an interrupt is generated.
Returns a word containing the number of baud rates available
Supplies one word of index numbers and reads the baud rate associated with that index.
Flushes buffer on write; undefined on read

One word containing flags:
IrDA capable Consumer IR capable ASK-IR capable Reserved

One word containing the type of IR:
Wired IrDA ConsumerIR Ask-IR Reserved

subsubsection.title: Generic IOCtl operations
subsubsection.p: The following IOCtl operations have been defined for generic operations :

item.p: Non-blocking operation. A word containing 0 for blocking operation, any other value indicating non-blocking operation
Buffer threshold. A word indicating a point in the buffer at which a notification will be raised.
Flush stream. No data; writing causes all pending data to be discarded
Timeout. Time in centiseconds before a blocking operation should be considered failed.

p.fixme: The IOCtl reason code numbers for the generic operations are not documented.

subsection.title: Filing system redeclaration
subsection.p: As a reminder, PRM 2-524 indicates that filing systems should redeclare themselves to FileSwitch when is issued. Some external filing systems do not do this and thus cannot cope when the FileSwitch module is restarted.

entry.register-use: Last handle, or -1 to start at first handle

exit.register-use: Stream status word, or preserved if no more handles exist
File handle, or -1 if no more handles exist
Filing system info word, or preserved if no more handles exist
